0.headline: SEBI paused Inox Clean Energy IPO over ongoing investigation into INOXGFL group entities, say sources
0.heading: SEBI paused Inox Clean Energy IPO over ongoing investigation into INOXGFL group entities, say sources
0.intro: The renewable energy company’s DRHP discloses scrutiny of Inox Green’s divestments, investigations into Inox Wind’s disclosures and transactions and a summons to promoter Devansh Jain over trading in PVR Inox shares
0.body:
The Securities and Exchange Board of India’s (SEBI's) decision to keep Inox Clean Energy’s proposed Rs 10,000-crore initial public offering (IPO) in abeyance was on account of ongoing investigations involving parent INOXGFL group entities, sources told Moneycontrol.

SEBI’s update on October 1 did not specify the reasons for the move, but sources said scrutiny around transactions through which the listed Inox Green Energy Services divested its shareholding in Inox Clean Energy and three subsidiaries drove the regulator’s action.

SEBI can keep observations in abeyance in specified circumstances involving investigations or inquiries into issuers, promoters, directors or group companies.

SEBI’s rules prescribe an initial 30-day abeyance for certain investigations, extendable by another 30 days in specified circumstances. The abeyance could be lifted after the initial 30-day period if the applicable regulatory conditions are met.

The proposed IPO comprises a Rs 8,000 crore fresh issue and a Rs 2,000 crore offer for sale by promoter Devansh Jain. Inox Clean Energy proposes to use Rs 6,000 crore of the fresh proceeds to repay debt.

Inox Clean Energy is promoted by the Vivek Jain-led INOXGFL Group, with his son, Devansh, serving as executive director. INOXGFL is separate from the similarly named INOX Group, which controls Inox Air Products and listed cryogenic-equipment manufacturer Inox India.

INOXGFL Group spans fluorochemicals, fluoropolymers, battery materials, wind and solar equipment manufacturing and renewable power generation.

Emails sent to Inox Clean Energy and SEBI had not elicited a response at the time of publication.

DRHP disclosures

The DRHP, dated September 29, discloses that SEBI sought information from Inox Green Energy Services in December on the difference between the Rs 290 crore consideration approved by its board and shareholders for selling Inox Clean Energy and the Rs 90 crore reflected as received in its FY25 standalone accounts.

Inox Clean Energy was formerly a wholly owned subsidiary of Inox Green Energy Services, which transferred its entire shareholding to IGREL Renewables on November 29, 2024. Following subsequent transfers to Jain family members, the holding is now principally with Devansh, jointly with Avarna Jain, according to the draft prospectus.

Inox Green told SEBI that the Rs 290 crore represented enterprise value, comprising approximately Rs 200 crore towards repayment of Inox Clean Energy’s Power Finance Corporation loan and Rs 90 crore in equity consideration. The transaction was authorised and the required stock exchange disclosures was made, it said.

SEBI also questioned the rationale behind divesting Inox Neo Energies, Flurry Wind Energy and Flutter Wind Energy to Inox Clean Energy at face value, particularly since Inox Neo subsequently raised around Rs 292 crore by issuing shares at Rs 265 apiece.

Inox Green said the subsidiaries had no operations or revenue-generating assets at the time of sale and the consideration reflected their book value. The divestments enabled it to focus on its core operations and maintenance business, it said.

SEBI sought further clarifications in February and March 2026 concerning two valuation reports dated October 20, 2023, issued by the same valuer, which showed materially different valuations of Inox Clean Energy.

The regulator asked which report was considered by the audit committee and board and shared with shareholders and auditors.

Inox Green attributed the difference to an "inadvertent omission" of the debt adjustment in the initial report. It said the corrected report was used for approvals and audit and sharing the earlier version with the proxy adviser was inadvertent. Its last disclosed response was dated April 8, 2026.

The DRHP SAYS no show-cause notice, order or adjudication proceedings were initiated by SEBI against Inox Green as of the filing date and added that a favourable conclusion to the inquiry could not be assured.

Other SEBI issues

Separately, Inox Wind received SEBI summons over financial disclosures and business transactions, the prospectus says. Devansh Jain and independent director Bindu Saxena attended personal hearings. Inox Wind also received queries relating to investigations into suspected insider trading by certain entities in its shares.

Jain received a separate summons concerning SEBI’s investigation into trading in PVR Inox shares for potential securities-law violations. The DRHP says Inox Wind and Jain have responded to SEBI.

1.headline: IPO euphoria giving way to greater scrutiny of valuations: JSA’s Arka Mookerjee
1.heading: IPO euphoria giving way to greater scrutiny of valuations: JSA’s Arka Mookerjee
1.intro: Companies offering good value can still attract demand despite secondary-market volatility, the co-head of equity capital markets at law firm JSA tells Moneycontrol
1.body:
The recent euphoria in the IPO market is giving way to more selective investing, marked by a greater scrutiny of valuations and pressure on issuers to rationalise pricing, Arka Mookerjee, co-head of equity capital markets at law firm JSA, has said.

The shift comes even as market tracker Prime Database shows that 69 companies launched IPOs over the last three months and raised over Rs 90,000 crore.

In an interview to Moneycontrol, Mookerjee said companies offering good value can still attract demand despite secondary-market volatility. Manufacturing, healthcare and businesses using AI to improve operations are more likely to tap public markets, he said. Here are the edited excerpts of the interview:

India’s IPO pipeline remains substantial but market volatility has made issuers more cautious about timing and valuations. How do you see IPO activity developing over the next 12–18 months?

There is a gradual movement of investor reaction from euphoria to discernment for IPOs. There is also an understanding that IPOs are not linked to the secondary market volatility and that it will be possible for issuers to bring our initial offers even when there is volatility. Given the movement towards quality investing, IPOs by companies offering a good value proposition will continue to remain in demand.

The subsidence of euphoria has also lead to greater scrutiny of valuations and demand for rationalisation of the valuations sought by issuers.

Which sectors are expected to lead IPO activity over the next year?

Given the speed at which info-tech or AI is evolving, it is unlikely that issuers with these as their primary area of activity will be able to match fund requirements with the longer timeline of public fundraising. Manufacturing linked entities or healthcare or entities which are utilising AI to streamline processes are more likely to tap markets.

QIPs have revived this year. What is driving the resurgence? Are companies increasingly raising equity to finance capital expenditure rather than to reduce debt or strengthen their balance sheets?

QIP activity is intrinsically linked to volatility in the secondary market. While the indices have been exhibiting volatility, funding requirements of companies have not disappeared. The usual reasons including meeting public shareholding requirements, funding capital expenditure and debt retirement remain in vogue. There doesn’t seem to be any clear signs that a particular objective is taking priority over the other.

Do you expect large private-sector banks and other financial institutions to tap the market through QIPs over the next six to 12 months?

The funding cycle of financial institutions is also underway and we expect to see the banks and FIs continuing to tap equity and debt markets to strengthen balance sheets. Given the clear signs of increasing use of debt to finance personal expenses, there is a possibility of financing institutions moving to raise funds soon.

Are more companies considering SEBI’s confidential pre-filing route? 

There is a greater acceptance of the confidential filing route as compared to the initial days, when this was introduced. Some regulatory clarifications such as shortening of timelines for OFS share eligibility, while SEBI review happens in parallel is one of the clearest changes which has helped make this route popular.

Additionally, greater possibility of discussions of regulatory issues in parallel with the draft document review is making this route a preferred route for companies which do not have a clear path to IPO.

The benefits of companies being able to keep their data private while their marketing and regulatory review is underway is one of the reasons that SEBI had clearly outlined and that has played out and continues to remain a useful consideration for companies looking to go public.

Which emerging regulatory concerns from SEBI are holding up IPOs?


The regulator has remained extremely responsive to market demands while keeping the scrutiny levels at par. While SEBI is a regulator charged with oversight, there has been a long held investor view that SEBI review equals to SEBI approval. This causes a significant regulatory review timeline expansion as SEBI is deeply cognisant of investor trust reposed in SEBI review.

Objects and capital structure remain key focus areas for SEBI. Promoter identification has become more streamlined but challenges on exemptions for promoter group remain. In addition to these, clarity on SEBI processes for deemed public offers would be welcome, since the withdrawal of the earlier exit offer circular.

Which regulatory changes would capital markets lawyers want SEBI to consider to simplify the IPO process? Are reforms also needed for QIPs, InvITs, REITs and other fundraising instruments?

Codification of the exchange guidelines on promoter identification and commencing grant of exemptions for promoter group would be welcome changes. Given that SEBI has already significantly reduced the timelines and requirements for rights issues and preferential allotments, further changes in routes may not be required.

For InvITs and REITs, clarification on end of life actions and winding up of these vehicles would be useful.

How is JSA expanding its equity capital markets practice and what are its core growth objectives?

JSA has historically grown organically and we continue to try and promote internal talent. Given the growth in markets, we have been lucky to be able to source talent from across the market and we add senior resources opportunistically. We remain market leaders in the InvIT space and have been working to expand our presence in other pooled investment vehicles. Our equity practice remains one of India’s oldest and we continue to be humbled by the faith clients repose in us.

As a practice we remain cognisant of client requirements and would like to become the single largest capital markets practice in this country by volume and value in the coming decade.

Manufacturing and healthcare sectors are expected to lead future public listings, while QIP activity revives amid steady corporate funding needs.

2.headline: Nityas Gems and Jewellery IPO allotment today on BSE, NSE and registrar — check latest GMP
2.heading: Nityas Gems and Jewellery IPO allotment today on BSE, NSE and registrar — check latest GMP
2.intro: The share allotment for the Nityas Gems and Jewellery IPO is expected to be finalised today, October 6, following the close of its three-day bidding process. Investors who applied for the Rs 108.35-crore public issue can check their allotment status through the BSE and NSE websites or the IPO registrar, Bigshare Services.
2.body:
The share allotment for the Nityas Gems and Jewellery IPO is expected to be finalised today, October 6, following the close of its three-day bidding process. Investors who applied for the Rs 108.35-crore public issue can check their allotment status through the BSE and NSE websites or the IPO registrar, Bigshare Services.

The IPO received bids for 3,25,80,400 shares against 1,44,56,000 shares on offer, resulting in an overall subscription of 2.25 times, according to data from the stock exchanges.

Retail investors led the demand, with their portion subscribed 4.04 times. The Non-Institutional Investors (NIIs) category was subscribed 2.05 times, while the Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIBs) portion received 1.06 times subscription. The employee portion was subscribed 2.82 times.

Read Also: Vishal Nirmiti IPO allotment today; check status on BSE, NSE and registrar

How to check Nityas Gems and Jewellery IPO allotment status on BSE

Step 1. Visit the BSE IPO application status page at https://www.bseindia.com/investors/appli_check
Step 2. Select Equity as the issue type.
Step 3. Select Nityas Gems and Jewellery Ltd. from the issue name dropdown.
Step 4. Enter the application number or PAN.
Step 5. Complete the captcha.
Step 6. Click Search to view the allotment status.

How to check Nityas Gems and Jewellery IPO allotment status on NSE

1. Visit the NSE IPO bid page at https://www.nseindia.com/invest/check-trades-bids-verify-ipo-bids
2. Select Equity &amp; SME IPO bid details.
3. Select NITYAS from the company symbol dropdown.
4. Enter the PAN or application number.
5. Click Submit to check the status.

How to check Nityas Gems and Jewellery IPO allotment status on Bigshare

Step 1. Go to the Bigshare IPO status portal at https://www.bigshareonline.com/ipo_allotment.html
Step 2. Select Nityas Gems and Jewellery from the company list.
Step 3. Choose the relevant option, such as PAN, application number or DP/Client ID.
Step 4. Enter the required details.
Step 5. Click Search to view the allotment status.

The company is scheduled to finalise the basis of allotment on October 6. Refunds for unsuccessful applicants and credit of shares to successful bidders are expected on October 7.

The grey market premium (GMP) for Nityas Gems and Jewellery stood at Rs 1, or around 1.33 percent, in the latest InvestorGain update. Based on the upper end of the IPO price band of Rs 75, the GMP indicates an estimated listing price of around Rs 76.

GMP is an unofficial indicator based on grey market activity. It is not regulated by stock exchanges and can change before listing. The actual listing price may differ from the GMP-implied price.

The IPO was open for subscription from September 30 to October 5. The price band was fixed at Rs 70-75 per share, with a lot size of 200 shares. At the upper end of the price band, retail investors had to invest Rs 15,000 for one lot.

The book-built issue comprises an entirely fresh issue of 1.44 crore shares, with no offer-for-sale component. The issue size is approximately Rs 108.35 crore at the upper end of the price band.

Check IPO News Here

The company plans to deploy Rs 70 crore from the net IPO proceeds towards working capital requirements. The balance is earmarked for general corporate purposes.

Choice Capital Advisors is the book-running lead manager, while Bigshare Services Private Limited is the registrar to the issue.

The shares of Nityas Gems and Jewellery are scheduled to list on the BSE and NSE on October 8, 2026. The basis of allotment is expected to be finalised on October 6, followed by refunds and Demat credit on October 7.

About Nityas Gems and Jewellery

Nityas Gems and Jewellery is a Gujarat-based jewellery manufacturer that designs and manufactures lab-grown diamond-studded gold jewellery. The company primarily follows a business-to-business model, supplying jewellery to organised and standalone retailers and wholesalers across multiple states.

The company also has a direct-to-consumer presence through its subsidiary, Ayaani Diamonds and Jewellery, which operates an omnichannel retail business. Its operations include manufacturing as well as the sale of jewellery through B2B and D2C channels.
